questions: Does reducing wheel_radius to 0.025 m lower max_error on the s-bend and slalom below the 0.06 m floor, compared with 0.030 m in iteration 8?
Does line_loss_events fall toward 0 on the s-bend and slalom, or does it stay at 1 per run? If it stays, at what point on the track is the line lost?
Does steering_oscillation fall below about 0.17 on the s-bend and slalom, or does it rise?
Does progress drop noticeably on the oval, and by how much? If speed is now the binding limit, is there a radius between 0.025 and 0.030 m that keeps both control and progress?
feedback_request.requested_changes_if_any: If progress falls sharply and the robot still leaves the track at about 0.06 m, say whether the error is driven by speed or by the controller's response. If the slalom oscillation rises, state whether a wheel_radius of 0.0275 m is a better compromise.

intent: Change only wheel_radius, from 0.030 to 0.025 m, on top of the iteration 8 design (0.4 kg, 0.08 m track, seven sensors at 20 mm spacing, y = 0.07 m, 12 mm footprints). The aim is to reduce ground speed so the controller can hold the line at the 0.06 m floor on the s-bend and slalom. Expected: max_error at or below about 0.06 m on those tracks, line_loss_events falling toward 0, and steering_oscillation at or below about 0.17. Progress may fall on the oval, and I accept that trade-off if off-track departures are delayed.
learning: Mass at 0.4 kg (the minimum) gave the largest gain since sensor lead: the score rose 3.4 with the oval, s-bend and slalom all improving. Yaw inertia is therefore an active constraint. Track is at its minimum, so the next test isolates ground speed through wheel_radius. The 0.06 m floor and body width are fixed, and sensor span, lead and footprint are settled.
rationale: Iteration 8 (0.4 kg mass) is the best result so far at 71.37, up from 67.95. Lighter mass helped all three tracks: oval 84.1 to 86.4, s-bend 72.6 to 76.6, slalom 47.1 to 51.1. Yaw inertia was a real constraint, and mass is now at its 0.4 kg minimum, so that lever is spent. Every run still ends off track with max_error about 0.062-0.066 m, just past the fixed 0.06 m floor. Body width cannot relax that floor (max(0.06, 0.0125 + W/4) is 0.06 m for any allowed body), and body_length has no effect on dynamics, so neither is a lever. Wheel_track is already at its 0.08 m minimum. The line-loss count on the s-bend and slalom is still about 1 per run, and steering oscillation rose on those tracks (0.173 and 0.168), which suggests the robot is arriving at the edge of the line too fast for the controller to correct. The remaining untested geometry lever is wheel_radius, which sets ground speed per wheel rotation. I reduce it from 0.030 to 0.025 m. That lowers top speed and lateral lag through bends, giving the controller more time per unit of error, and the feedback from iteration 8 asked for this test. I keep mass, track, body, sensor row (seven sensors, 20 mm spacing, y = 0.07 m) and 12 mm footprints fixed so the effect is isolated. Expected result: max_error and line-loss events fall on the s-bend and slalom, and steering oscillation stays at or below about 0.17. Risk: slower ground speed reduces progress within the 3 s limit, so the score could fall on the oval if the robot would otherwise have covered more track.
